title: Intermediate Backend Engineer, Cells Infrastructure
description: div class= content-intro p GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. /p p The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values nbsp;and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. a href= https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI Co-create the future with us /a as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. /p p * em Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. /em /p /div h2 An overview of this role /h2 p As an Intermediate Backend Engineer on GitLab's Cells Infrastructure team, you'll help build the architecture that lets GitLab.com scale horizontally. Cells splits GitLab.com into independent units, each with its own application and data stack, behind a shared routing layer. /p p You'll build the services and application changes that make Cells work: the control plane that tracks cells and organizations, the routing logic that sends each request to the right cell, and the changes inside the GitLab application that keep data unique and consistent across cells. Your work will directly support moving customer organizations onto Cells, one of GitLab's most important scaling initiatives. /p p You'll work across Go, Ruby on Rails, and TypeScript. /p h2 What you’ll do /h2 ul li value= 1 Design, build, and maintain the Cells control plane, a Go service using gRPC (remote procedure calls) and backed by Cloud Spanner that tracks cells, organizations, and globally unique resources. /li li value= 2 Extend the global routing layer, written in TypeScript on Cloudflare Workers, so requests reach the right cell. This includes classifying requests by path, namespace, and token, and supporting more protocols and services. /li li value= 3 Make changes in the GitLab Rails application so it works across multiple cells: claiming globally unique resources, propagating organization context, and keeping cell-local data consistent. /li li value= 4 Design application programming interfaces (APIs) and data models with correctness, idempotency, and backward compatibility in mind, so changes can roll out safely across a fleet of cells. /li li value= 5 Write thorough automated tests, including unit, integration, and end-to-end tests, and improve test coverage and reliability across the services we own. /li li value= 6 Instrument your services with OpenTelemetry for metrics, logs, and distributed tracing. Help define service level objectives (SLOs) and take part in on-call for the services you build. /li li value= 7 Work with product teams to make their features cell-compatible, and review their changes for Cells correctness. /li li value= 8 Write clear design documents, architecture decision records, and documentation, and take part in code review as both author and reviewer. /li /ul h2 What you’ll bring /h2 ul li value= 1 Professional experience building and running backend services in production, including monitoring, debugging, and incident response. You've instrumented services with OpenTelemetry and used distributed tracing to debug requests across service boundaries. /li li value= 2 Proficiency in Go, or strong experience in another backend language and willingness to work in Go daily. /li li value= 3 Experience with Ruby on Rails and TypeScript, or the willingness to become productive in both. Our control plane is written in Go, the GitLab application in Rails, and our edge routing layer in TypeScript. /li li value= 4 Experience designing APIs using gRPC or Representational State Transfer (REST), and working with relational or distributed databases, including schema design, transactions, and migrations. /li li value= 5 A strong understanding of distributed-systems fundamentals, such as consistency, idempotency, concurrency, retries, and failure handling. /li li value= 6 Solid grounding in engineering best practices: test-driven development, small iterative merge requests, thorough code review, feature flags for safe rollouts, and observable, well-documented code. /li li value= 7 Experience working effectively in distributed, all-remote teams: you default to asynchronous, written-first communication, document decisions in issues and merge requests, hand off work cleanly across time zones, and stay transparent about progress and blockers. /li li value= 8 If you've worked with Cloud Spanner, Cloudflare Workers, Kubernetes, multi-tenant or sharded architectures, or contributed to GitLab, that's a plus, not a requirement. /li /ul h2 About the team /h2 p The Cells Infrastructure team is part of GitLab's Scale amp; Architecture organization, which builds and operates the core services that let GitLab.com grow. title: Enterprise Agentic AI Architect
description: div class= content-intro p strong About Coursera + Udemy /strong /p p Coursera and Udemy are now one company, bringing together two mission-driven brands to create the world’s most powerful platform for turning learning into progress. Together, we help more than 300 million learners and 12,000+ enterprise customers build the skills they need for a world being reshaped by AI. Read more about the combined company by visiting our nbsp; a href= https://blog.coursera.org/coursera-and-udemy-are-now-one-company-creating-the-worlds-most-comprehensive-skills-platform/ target= _blank blog /a . /p p strong Why join us now? /strong /p p AI is transforming how people learn, work, and grow, and the need for new skills has never been greater. Coursera brings trusted content and credentials from leading university and industry partners, while Udemy brings a dynamic skills marketplace and global network of real-world experts. By combining these strengths, we can connect more people and organizations to the skills they need, when they need them. /p p strong Shape what comes next /strong /p p By joining our team, you’ll have the opportunity to reshape how the world learns and applies skills—and help millions of people participate in the new economy. Bring your ideas, expertise, and perspective to meaningful work that can make a difference at global scale. /p /div h3 About the Role /h3 p Coursera’s AI adoption has moved fast — engineering teams code AI-first, dozens of internal tools have shipped, and functions across the business are building their own AI agents and automations. The next phase requires something different: a shared technical foundation that lets many teams build safely and cost-effectively at scale, instead of each team solving governance, security, and cost from scratch. /p p This role owns that foundation. The Senior Agentic AI Architect Lead designs and builds the core architecture that Coursera’s AI Builders and business pods will run on — so that a small team (a Business Product Owner, a Process Expert, an IT Product Owner, and an AI Engineer) can redesign a workflow and ship an AI-native solution in weeks, not months. /p p This is a hands-on architecture role, not a pure strategy role: you will be building, not just advising. /p h3 What You’ll Own /h3 ul li strong Context amp; Semantic Architecture - /strong Design how AI agents access and understand Coursera’s internal data and knowledge, so agents retrieve the right information rather than guessing or over-fetching. Establish reusable patterns for RAG, semantic search, structured data access, and enterprise context, partnering with the Data team on existing data models and pipelines. /li li strong Agentic Architecture amp; Harness Engineering - /strong Design reusable patterns for agent orchestration, tool use, multi-step workflows, state management, and human-in-the-loop decisions. Build the engineering harness around agents, including testing, evaluation, guardrails, retries, observability, and failure recovery, so agentic solutions are reliable and production-ready. /li li strong Governance Architecture - /strong Build technical guardrails that enforce—not just document—who can build what, what data and systems an agent can access, and what gets logged for audit and review. Establish standards for agent ownership, lifecycle management, and production readiness. /li li strong Security Architecture - /strong Design defenses specific to agentic AI, including agent identity and access control, least-privilege permissions, prompt injection, data leakage, secure credentials, and safe tool execution. Coordinate with Security to extend existing enterprise security standards. /li li strong Self-Serve AI Development (“Vibe Coding”) with CI/CD Automation - /strong Extend and mature Coursera’s self-serve deployment path so AI-assisted, conversational development ships through automated testing, security checks, and evaluation gates—safe by default, not safe by manual gatekeeping. /li li strong LLM Cost amp; Performance Optimization - /strong Design caching, model routing (matching task complexity to the right-sized model), token and context optimization, and usage monitoring so AI adoption can scale without costs growing linearly. Establish cost, latency, quality, and usage metrics. /li li strong Agent Operating Model amp; Adoption - /strong Define agent ownership, lifecycle management, production-readiness standards, adoption metrics, and reusable patterns so business teams can scale AI capabilities consistently across functions. Measure success through usage, workflow outcomes, productivity, quality, and business value. /li li strong Architecture Strategy amp; Execution - /strong Turn ambiguous business problems into scalable technical direction, practical roadmaps, architecture decisions, and production delivery. /li li strong Enterprise Systems amp; Integration Architecture - /strong Design AI solutions that understand dependencies across enterprise systems, business processes, integrations, and downstream impacts.
